A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DERL work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original prediction, physical-consistency, generalization, distillation, and timing results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices A, D, and E.

after.justification: v2 reports original empirical results, including the retained experiments and new Navier–Stokes, temporal-transfer, and noise/step-size experiments.

M1.justification: The derivative-learning loss, boundary/initial-condition terms, derivative distillation, and higher-order variants remain unchanged. Temporal transfer applies the existing incremental protocol to another scenario. The earlier 'fine-tune' configuration is renamed 'continual'.

E1.justification: v2 adds stationary two-dimensional Navier–Stokes Kovasznay flow and incremental KdV transfer to longer time horizons. The latter differs from the retained whole-domain KdV distillation experiment. Appendix F additionally evaluates noisy derivative targets alongside the existing physical tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in corresponding experiments, including OUTL, OUTL+PINN, SOB, PINN controls, and HNN/LNN. The new Navier–Stokes and temporal-transfer experiments reuse existing comparator sets; the sensitivity study compares DERL with the existing SOB baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols include Navier–Stokes training/testing grids with spacing 0.01/0.005 and vorticity evaluation; three KdV time intervals trained for 30,000/30,000/40,000 steps with a matched total-budget PINN control; and step-size/noise sweeps at 0.001, 0.01, and 0.05. These are additional protocols, rather than demonstrated reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds systematic noise and finite-difference sensitivity tests for Allen–Cahn and the damped pendulum, replacing reliance on a qualitative caveat and fixed-step experiments. New temporal-transfer learning curves and the no-distillation control examine optimization stagnation and forgetting.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The Gaussian noise parameter in v2 controls experimental perturbations; it does not represent uncertainty in reported performance estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds Navier–Stokes results, temporal-transfer results, and sensitivity Tables 15–16. For example, new Table 6 reports KdV prediction errors of 0.03331/0.02379 for DERL from-scratch/continual versus 0.09801 for PINN-full. Retained tables preserve their values apart from equivalent scaling/rounding. The fine-tuned parameter-space winner map in v1 Figure 20 is removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit higher-order ODE/state-system formulation and mathematical definitions for the Kovasznay solution and vorticity. The DERL convergence theorems, their assumptions, and the proofs in Appendices B and C remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The principal derivative-learning, convergence, and physical-knowledge-distillation contributions are retained. v2 explicitly extends the claimed transfer capability to longer time horizons, alongside the existing spatial-domain and parameter extensions.

C2.justification: v1 explicitly identifies susceptibility to noise and large finite-difference steps; v2 instead emphasizes robustness in Appendix F, despite degradation in its tables. v2 also adds an interpretation of temporal incremental training as alleviating PINN optimization problems and explicitly reserves longer-sequence continual learning and forgetting mitigation for future work.

D1.justification: v2 supplies technical details for the additions, including the analytic Kovasznay solution and temporal-transfer architecture, collocation sampling, learning-rate schedule, and loss weights. Existing implementation, hardware, and tuning disclosures remain largely unchanged, and no code/data release is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Drazin and Riley, Pascanu et al., Son et al.'s Sobolev training for PINNs, and Wang et al.'s neural-tangent-kernel analysis. It expands numerical-method background and clarifies positioning relative to neural operators and continual learning while retaining the central novelty argument.

P1.justification: The introduction and transfer narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves ahead of the method into an expanded Background and Related Works section; mathematical explanations expand, transfer sections are reorganized, and the standalone main-text Limitations section disappears as noise discussion moves into Appendix F.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, typography, and table formatting, including powers-of-ten headers and a consolidated transfer table. It adds Navier–Stokes and temporal-transfer plots and sensitivity tables. v1 Figure 4 is split and relocated to appendix Figures 14 and 16; the fine-tuned parameter-transfer map is removed.

improvement.justification: The temporal-transfer and sensitivity experiments strengthen empirical support and quantify behavior that v1 only discussed. Expanded background and protocol descriptions also aid assessment. These gains are tempered by the overly broad robustness interpretation despite Table 16's large-step degradation, inconsistent vorticity formulas between Section 4.1 and Appendix D.3, and removal of the fine-tuned parameter-transfer map.
